parts.value_and_ratings: 30.0 kohm (Rf), 0.1% (B), 25 ppm/K (E), 0.1 W at 85 C, thin film, AEC-Q200; V = punched carrier tape, 4 mm pitch, 5000 pcs
parts.calculation: DAC80501Z Equation 1: VOUT = code/65536 x VREFIO/DIV x GAIN. With REF-DIV=1 (DIV=2) and BUFF-GAIN=1 (GAIN=2) the full scale is 2.5 V. OPA197 non-inverting gain G = 1 + 30.0k/10.0k = 4.000, so the output reaches 10.00 V nominal. Tolerance: dG/G = 0.75 x (+/-0.1% +/-0.1%) = +/-0.15%. The internal reference is 2.4975-2.5025 V (+/-0.1%), the DAC full-scale error with REF-DIV=1 is +/-0.06 %FSR, and OPA197 Vos of +/-100 uV times 4 is 0.4 mV. Worst case at 25 C: FS(min) = 10 x 0.999 x 0.9994 x 0.9985 - 0.0004, about 9.968 V; FS(max) is about 10.031 V. Over temperature the reference adds 5 ppm/K, DAC FS 2 ppm/K, and resistor ratio mismatch up to 0.75 x 50 = 37.5 ppm/K. At dT = 45 K that is about -0.2% more, taking the minimum to about 9.95 V. Swing budget at ANALOG_12V minimum 11.4 V: output at most 10.031 V at about 1.25 mA (10 k receiver plus 40 k feedback), leaving 1.37 V headroom. OPA197 section 6.7 gives maximum swing-from-rail of 125 mV at RL = 10 k and 500 mV at 2 k, so the margin is at least 0.87 V. Rf dissipation is (7.5 V)^2 / 30 k = 1.9 mW.

groups.engineering_notes:
Summary: 12 parts selected across 11 rows (analog_gain has two resistors). rx_termination was already selected in the rx_abz block. watchdog_timing is infeasible with the TPS3431 in the ledger.

Nothing was written inside the controller workspace. Scratch datasheet copies and extracted text are in C:/Users/Gluis/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/C--Users-Gluis-OneDrive-Documents-ChatGPT-Controller/280553e2-7c85-48b3-a5fa-96a4c2e06e60/scratchpad/ro/. I re-read the ledger files (mtime 04:48:46), the tx_six and rx_abz BOMs (unchanged) and the encoder_power BOM (updated at 14:57, no conflicting passive MPNs) before reporting.

1) WATCHDOG IS INFEASIBLE AS SPECIFIED. With TPS3431SDRBR the shortest external timeout is 56.77 / 62.74 / 68.7 ms at CCWD = 100 pF (datasheet Table 8-3; Eq. 1 is 77.4 x C + 55 ms). The 20 ms maximum cannot be met, and the ledger limit was not changed. Candidate fix, not applied: TI TPS3851 'S' standard-timing parts (TPS3851G18SDRBR, TPS3851G33SDRBR, TPS3851G50SDRBR are active in the TI SBVS300B orderable addendum). Their Eq. 1 is tWD = 3.23 x CCWD(nF) + 0.381 ms, with boundaries 0.905x and 1.095x. With a 3.3 nF +/-5% C0G capacitor: min = 0.905 x (3.23 x 3.135 + 0.381) = 9.51 ms; typ = 11.04 ms; max = 1.095 x (3.23 x 3.465 + 0.381) = 12.67 ms. That meets > 5 ms and <= 20 ms. Caveats: TPS3851 is a supervisor as well as a watchdog, so pinout and footprint differ from TPS3431. On IO_3V3 the G33 threshold (3.168 V +/-0.8%, release up to about 3.22 V) conflicts with the 3.2 V rail minimum, so G18 or a different supervision split would be needed. Changing the watchdog MPN, footprint and permission design needs a separate ledger decision.

2) DAC80501 CONFIGURATION. The '2.5 V reference, gain 1' decision works only as a net x1: REF-DIV=1 (divide by 2) with BUFF-GAIN=1 (x2). Datasheet section 7.3 limits VREFIO to 0.5 x VDD when REF-DIV=0, so the internal 2.5 V reference needs VDD >= 5.0 V in that mode. At the ANALOG_5V minimum of 4.85 V that is violated, and section 8.3.2 says an improper divider setting raises a reference alarm that forces VOUT to 0 V. The POR default (REF-DIV=0, BUFF-GAIN=1, for a 0-5 V range) is therefore a fail-to-zero configuration below 5.0 V. Gateware must write GAIN register 4h (REF-DIV=1, BUFF-GAIN=1) before output is enabled, and should check the alarm. BUFF-GAIN=0 with REF-DIV=0 is not an output range listed in the section 7.5 VO table. With REF-DIV=1 and BUFF-GAIN=1, full scale is 2.5 V and DAC headroom is 4.85 - 2.5025 = 2.35 V, against a 0.3 V spec at 10 mA. The ledger text 'internal2.5Vref gain1' should say this explicitly.

3) ANALOG FULL-SCALE ACCURACY. 30.0k/10.0k 0.1% gives 10.00 V nominal. Untrimmed worst case is about 9.968-10.031 V at 25 C, and down to about 9.95 V over a 45 K temperature swing (discrete-resistor ratio drift dominates). If 10.0 V must be guaranteed, the options are software calibration with a code clamp, a slightly higher gain with a clamp, or a ratio-matched network. The ledger target was not changed.

OPA197 swing budget: 11.4 V - 10.031 V = 1.37 V headroom, against at most 125 mV (10 k) or 500 mV (2 k) swing-from-rail in OPA197 section 6.7, which is ample. At the zero end, the single-supply output sits 5-25 mV above ground unloaded, plus DAC zero-code error of +/-1.5 mV x 4. The output is therefore not exactly 0 V, and the physical zero clamp is still required.

4) ISO1212 RTHR. TI requires 0.25 W MELF parts (section 8.2.1.2.1). MMA 0204 at 1 k has a 1.2/50 us rating of only about 0.7-0.8 kV, read from the datasheet graph. It is adequate if the SMF36A input TVS clamps ahead of it; surge coordination remains open.

5) VERIFICATION METHOD. DigiKey, Mouser, Newark, Farnell, TME, Octopart and TrustedParts returned 403, timeouts or resets to automated fetches. Manufacturer sources were opened directly: Vishay doc 20035 (CRCW), Vishay doc 28963 (MMA 0204), the Panasonic ERA-xA PDF, and Samsung SEM product pages. Each exact ordering code was decoded from, or shown on, those sources, and its existence was cross-checked in search-engine results for distributor listings of that exact MPN. No prices or stock were recorded. Selecting these MPNs does not qualify any circuit: SI, surge and EMC, thermal, layout, ERC/DRC and physical measurement are all still open.

parts.calculation: AN006 v6.6 Table 1 gives T20 BGA256 a maximum single-image size of 5,255,968 bits, including an optional header of up to 1 kB. 32 Mbit / 5.256 Mbit = 6.38 images of capacity. Four CBSEL images (4 x 5.256 = 21.0 Mbit) would still fit with 11 Mbit left for user data. AN006 'Selecting the Right SPI Flash Device' lists the Winbond W25Q family as supported. It requires 3-byte addressing, and the device supports that (32 Mbit < 128 Mbit, so there is no 4-byte mode issue). Commands: the T20 datasheet v6.0 (Configuration section) says the FPGA sends a release from power-down, waits at least 30 us, then fast-reads (0Bh) from 24'h000000. W25Q32JV tRES1 is 3 us max (datasheet section 9), so this is covered. Clock: T20 Table 117 fMAX_M is 26 MHz max (DIV4), well below the 133 MHz FR. Voltage: 2.7-3.6 V covers the ledger IO_3V3 range of 3.2-3.4 V. AN006 requires the flash voltage to equal the VCCIO of the configuration bank, which is 3.3 V here. Configuration time at x1 and 20 MHz typ = 5.256 Mbit / 20 MHz = 263 ms (at the 14 MHz minimum it is 375 ms). The flash power-up requirement (VCC(min) to /CS low, tVSL 20 us) is met because CRESET_N is held by the supervisor.
parts.verified_how: I downloaded and read the Winbond W25Q32JV datasheet (Rev G, 2018-03-27). Section 11.1 lists W25Q32JVSSIQ as a valid 12-digit product number (SOIC-8 208 mil, I grade, QE=1 fixed). I checked the instruction table (ABh, 0Bh, 3Bh, 6Bh with 24-bit address), the 133 MHz FR at 3.0-3.6 V, and tVSL/tRES1. The LCSC page C179173 confirms Winbond W25Q32JVSSIQ, SOIC-8-208mil, 32 Mbit, 2.7-3.6 V, -40 to 85 C, 133 MHz. Compatibility was cross-checked against Efinix AN006 v6.6 Table 1, Table 8 and Table 26, and the T20 datasheet DST20-v6.0 Table 117.

The ledger reserves active SPI x1 ('activeconfigurationSPI4plusstraps'), and T20 datasheet Table 67 note 13 says F256 does not support multi-image in x1 mode. A golden/fallback image therefore needs either x2/x4 wiring (CBUS change plus CDI2/CDI3 routing) or AN010 internal reconfiguration. Also open: CCK/CDI SI at the chosen DIV setting, factory programming method (JTAG-bridge flash loader vs. PCBWay pre-programming, and the SRP-bit caution in AN006), and the Efinity bitstream size of the actual design. Configuration time is not yet measured.

parts.calculation: T20 datasheet v6.0 Table 114 (PLL AC) requires a GPIO clock HIGH/LOW pulse width of at least 2.25 ns and input long-term jitter of at most 800 ps pk-pk. At 50 MHz (T = 20 ns) the worst-case duty of 45 % gives a 9.0 ns minimum pulse, which is 4x the 2.25 ns limit. The 1 ps RMS phase jitter (12 kHz-5 MHz) is about 14 ps pk-pk at a 14-sigma estimate, far below 800 ps. The datasheet does not specify long-term jitter directly, so treat this as an estimate. FIN of 50 MHz is inside the 10-200 MHz core/GPIO PLL input range. Frequency error of +/-50 ppm means the 5 ms RTL watchdog (250,000 cycles) varies by +/-0.25 us, and step timing error is 50 ppm. The ledger step limits and the RTL rate cap (195312.5 steps/s = 50 MHz x 0x01000000 / 2^32) scale by the same 50 ppm; that is not a limit change. Start-up of 5 ms max happens while CRESET_N/configuration is still running (about 263 ms at x1, 20 MHz), but the user clock domain must still stay in reset until PLL lock (tLOCK 0.5 ms max) and tUSER have elapsed. The ledger already says 'reset release synchronized independently per clock domain'.

parts.value_and_ratings: 4-bit dual-supply transceiver, VCCA/VCCB 1.1-3.6 V, independent DIR per bit, active-low OE referenced to VCCA. Ioff is specified on both ports (+/-1 uA max at VI/VO 0-3.6 V with that port's VCC = 0 V). VCC-isolation feature: if either VCC is 0 V, both ports are Hi-Z. I/Os are 4.6 V tolerant. DIR1-3 = H (A->B would be FPGA->SBC), so set DIR per bit: CS/SCLK/MOSI use DIR = L (B->A, SBC -> FPGA), MISO uses DIR = H (A->B, FPGA -> SBC). OE pulled up with 10 k CRCW060310K0FKEA to VCCA (default disabled) and driven low only by a rails-OK signal after both supplies are stable. 33 ohm CRCW060333R0FKEA series source resistors at each of the 4 outputs. 10 k pull-up on FPGA-side CS so it idles inactive. 100 nF CL10B104KA8NNNC on each of VCCA and VCCB.
parts.calculation: The ledger requires <=5 MHz SPI mode 0 (100 ns half-period). Round-trip: SCLK buffer tpd 2.9 ns + FPGA clock-to-MISO (RTL-dependent; not known) + MISO buffer tpd 2.9 ns + 2 x 33 ohm RC is about 6 ns plus FPGA tco, against a 100 ns sample window, so the margin is large. Why OE is default off: TI SCES693I section 8.3 says OE must be tied to VCCA through a pull-up and not enabled until VCCA and VCCB are fully ramped. Efinix AN006 p.43 says not to drive Trion I/Os before VCCIO is up; VCC isolation guarantees this even if OE is low. Levels: FPGA 3.3 V LVCMOS VOH >= 2.4 V exceeds the AVC VIH of 2.0 V (VCC 3.0-3.6 V); AVC VOH >= 2.4 V into the SBC and FPGA (VIH 2.0 V). groups.engineering_notes:
Read-only run. No files inside the Controller tree were created or changed, and I ran no scripts there. Scratch files are only under .../scratchpad/ro/: t20ds.pdf/txt, an006.pdf/txt, pgm.pdf, tintf.pdf, t20brd.pdf, p4*.png, w25q32jv.pdf/txt, ecs2520mv.pdf/txt, we61201021621.pdf, avc4t774.pdf and avc.txt, and wroom1.pdf/txt. The ledger (hardware/electrical-design.json and bom-snapshot.csv, mtime 2026-09-28 04:48) still shows all seven assigned rows as required_unselected. Nothing under research/power-entry, hardware/encoder_power, hardware/rx_abz, hardware/tx_six, hardware/tx_bank or hardware/power_entry picks any of these parts. My passive choices follow the existing subsheet style: 0603 X7R 25 V caps and Vishay CRCW0603 resistors, with 0402 used only for the BGA bypass.

Rows with more than one MPN: fpga_decoupling (4 entries) and host_spi_buffer (2 entries) have one StructuredOutput entry per MPN under the same ledger_id. esp_decoupling_boot and fpga_jtag list their companion MPNs inside value_and_ratings.

Important findings and caveats:
(1) The Efinix 'Trion Hardware Design Checklist and Guidelines' could not be downloaded; every guessed URL version returned 404. The decoupling set therefore copies the official Efinix T20F256 development board schematic Rev 3.0, sheet 5: VCC 7x0.1 uF + 2x0.22 uF + 4.7 uF; VCCA with a bead plus 4.7 uF and 2x0.1 uF; VCCIO 14x0.1 uF + 8x0.22 uF + 4.7 uF. It must be re-checked against the checklist before freeze.
(2) The ledger reserves active SPI x1 ('activeconfigurationSPI4plusstraps'). T20 datasheet v6.0 Table 67 note 13 says F256 does not support multi-image in x1, so a golden-image or remote-update strategy needs x2/x4 wiring or AN010 internal reconfiguration. This is a decision for the user, not something I changed.
(3) T20 VIN max is VCCIO + 0.3 V, and AN006 forbids driving Trion I/Os before VCCIO is up. For that reason both buffers are SN74AVC4T774PWR dual-supply parts with Ioff and VCC isolation, instead of a single-rail 74LVC125, which could back-power an unpowered SBC through MISO. The request named 74LVC/LV families only as examples; this is a deliberate substitution.
(4) The T20 power-ramp constraint VCCIO/10 to 10 V/ms (Table 71), the recommended VCC-then-VCCIO sequence, and tCRESET_N >= 320 ns all belong to the unselected power_supervisor row. The recovery button must go to the supervisor MR input, not directly to CRESET_N.
(5) No electrical or motion limit was changed. A +/-50 ppm oscillator scales the RTL rate cap (195312.5 steps/s) and the 5 ms RTL watchdog by at most 50 ppm.
(6) Evidence level: datasheet and distributor-page desk selection only. There has been no ERC, DRC, SI/PDN simulation, Efinity power estimate, thermal analysis, or physical measurement, and nothing here is manufacturing-ready.

Sources opened: Efinix T20 datasheet DST20-v6.0 (efinixinc.com/docs/trion20-ds-v6.0.pdf), AN006 v6.6 (efinixinc.com/docs/an006-configuring-trion-fpgas-v6.6.pdf), Efinity Programmer UG v3.3 (efinixinc.com/docs/efinity-pgm-v3.3.pdf), T20F256 dev-board schematic (efinixinc.com/support/docsdl.php?s=ef&pn=T20F256-BRD-SCHM), Trion Interfaces UG v7.5 (elitestek.com mirror), and the manufacturer and LCSC pages listed per part.

parts.calculation: Supplied from CORE_5V. Threshold Vtrip = 0.4 V x (1 + Rtop/Rbot). Worst case uses 396-404 mV and a +/-0.2% divider ratio (0.1% RT parts). SVS-1 CORE_5V UV: 107k/10.0k gives 4.680 V nominal, 4.616-4.744 V (above AM26C31 4.5 V min, below 4.85 V rail min). SVS-4L CORE_1V2 UV: 19.1k/10.0k gives 1.164 V, 1.149-1.179 V. SVS-4H CORE_1V2 OV: 21.0k/10.0k gives 1.240 V, 1.224-1.256 V. SVS-2 IO_3V3 UV: 69.8k/10.0k gives 3.192 V, 3.149-3.235 V. SVS-3 ESP_3V3 UV: 66.5k/10.0k gives 3.060 V, 3.019-3.101 V. The 1.2 V and 3.3 V trip windows sit below Codex's TPS62901 regulation-only minima (1.185 V and 3.259 V in hardware/logic_power/design-envelope.json), so normal regulation should not cause nuisance resets. Sequencing wiring, per T20 DS 'Power Up Sequence' (VCC first, then VCCIO, then hold CRESET_N low for at least tCRESET_N = 320 ns): RESET1 (100k pull-up to CORE_5V) drives EN of the 1.2 V buck, the ESP buck and the esp_branch_limit switch. RESET4 (1.2 V window, 20 ms, 100k pull-up to CORE_5V) drives EN of the IO_3V3 buck. RESET2 (IO_3V3 UV, 20 ms, 10k pull-up to IO_3V3) drives CRESET_N. RESET3 (10k pull-up to ESP_3V3) drives ESP EN. MR has a 100k pull-up to CORE_5V. WDI goes to GND and WDO is left unconnected (TPS3431 remains the independent watchdog). SENSE leakage of +/-25 nA into about 10k gives under 0.3 mV error.

The OV high edge (1.256 V) is 6 mV above the T20 1.25 V recommended maximum (the absolute maximum is 1.42 V). Tightening either edge causes overlap with the regulator tolerance, so this needs review. Power-down order is not controlled: a 5 V collapse drops the 1.2 V EN before IO_3V3. EN abs-max of the TPS62901 at a 5.15 V pull-up was not checked (its datasheet was not read). RAILS_OK derivation for permission_logic, partial-power and backfeed paths, glitch filtering, the VDD 0.1 uF bypass MPN, and bench tests of sequence, ramp and brownout all remain open.

The core eFuse (TPS26630, RILIM 8.20k) limits at 1.97-2.43 A, which is at most 81% of rating and below the 110% no-open level, so the fuse does not open during eFuse-limited overload. TVS 10/1000 us pulse at 31 A: I2t = Ipk^2 x tau/2 = 0.69 A2s, far below 9.4 A2s, so no nuisance opening at the SMCJ30CA rated pulse. Coordination assumption (ISO 8820-style MINI curve, not read from the datasheet): opening in 5 s or less needs roughly 200% or more (at least 6 A prospective), and in 0.5 s or less roughly 350% (10.5 A). A source limited to 2-3 A (ledger 2 A; Codex proposes 3 A) will not clear this fuse. It is a backup for shorted eFuse, FET or TVS faults only when the source can deliver at least 6-10 A, and the wiring must withstand at least 135% x 3 A = 4.05 A for up to about 30 min.

groups.engineering_notes:
Work was read-only. Scratch datasheets are under C:/Users/Gluis/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/C--Users-Gluis-OneDrive-Documents-ChatGPT-Controller/280553e2-7c85-48b3-a5fa-96a4c2e06e60/scratchpad/ro/pwr/. Codex was writing concurrently (hardware/core_converter, field_power and logic_power appeared at 15:17-15:22), and I reported against those newest files. The canonical hardware/electrical-design.json (electrical-r0.1) still lists every assigned row as required_unselected, so the folder decisions are not yet integrated into the ledger.

Findings that are infeasible or conflict with the ledger (no limits changed):
(1) TPS62160 cannot meet the ledger rails. Its initial accuracy is +/-3% in PWM and -3.5%/+4% in power-save mode (Electrical Characteristics). That gives 1.164-1.236 V at 1.2 V, against the CORE_1V2 window of 1.17-1.23 V. At 3.3 V, power-save mode can reach 3.18 V, below the IO_3V3 minimum of 3.2 V.
(2) The TPS62160 fixed soft-start slope of about 25 mV/us (25 V/ms, section 8.4.1) exceeds the T20 maximum ramp of 10 V/ms (T20 DS Table 71/87). Both findings support Codex's switch to TPS62901 with SS/TR; the ledger components buck_* still say TPS62160DSGR.
(3) The main 5 V capacity is limited by the input path. At 18 V, 85% efficiency, a 2 A core entry and 0.06 A analog, CORE_5V can deliver at most about 5.94 A. The core eFuse (RILIM 8.20k) limits at 1.97-2.43 A input. A 7 A-or-more converter therefore gives no usable 7 A until the core source, wiring and eFuse are revised (Codex proposes a 3 A source).
(4) The field fuse must be at least 7.5 A (4.36 A / 0.75 = 5.81 A), so field wiring and terminals must withstand at least 10 A, more than the '6 A' capacity wording. With a 6 A current-limited PSU, and a 2-3 A core PSU, neither physical fuse will clear. Each is only a backup against high-prospective-current sources, and the shorted-eFuse/TVS case depends on the PSU.
(5) FIELD_5V can reach 5.15 V, but TPS4H160 logic, FAULT and THER pins are recommended at 5 V maximum (7 V absolute). I used 20k pull-ups for DIAG_EN and THER. The FAULT pull-up still reaches 5.15 V.
(6) No isolated channels remain for TPS4H160 DIAG_EN, SEL or SEH (14 of 16 are used). DIAG_EN is strapped on and CS goes to a local test point only.
(7) The field eFuse ILIM screening low of 4.42 A against a 4.36 A normal load leaves about 1.4% margin (Codex already flags this).

The 0.5 A output current-limit resistor is 2.67k (Eq. 4: 0.8 x 2500 / I). The drive-enable banks use 7.87k (0.254 A), keeping ledger quantity 4. The OMNI-BLOK SMD alternative is Littelfuse 0154003.DRT and 0154007.DR/DRT, but its 50 A @ 125 VDC interrupting rating is weak and the 0154007.DRT time-lag characteristic was not confirmed, so I followed Codex's 58 V MINI candidates. The fuse opening-time and rerating data are assumed ISO 8820-style curves because the Littelfuse PDF returned 403.

Evidence level: only source inspection and datasheet/distributor checks were done. No ERC, simulation, thermal or bench measurement was performed. Nothing here qualifies a circuit or makes it ready to manufacture.
